There have long been rumours that Apple is developing a brand-new all-glass iPhone design to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone next year. However, analysts at Jefferies believe that the device is no longer being actively developed.

Wall Street analysts say the major iPhone redesign planned to celebrate the 20th anniversary has been cancelled

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies has today downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform". Analyst Edison Lee (李裕光) said the possible cancellation of the 20th-anniversary iPhone redesign is one of the main reasons behind the move.

The crux of this downgrade lies in the suspected cancellation of Apple's all-glass iPhone. Although reports dating back to 2025 suggested the project was in development, with rumours of an earliest launch in 2027, Apple has never commented on the speculation. However, Apple quietly filed a patent for a "six-sided glass enclosure" as early as 2019. Jefferies had previously considered the launch of an all-glass iPhone to be a possibility, but Edison Lee believes R&D has been halted. According to the analyst, supply chain checks indicate the project was scrapped due to excessively low yield rates. Edison Lee views this decision as a "major setback for pushing higher-priced iPhones amid soaring memory costs." Had the device indeed launched in September 2027 to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, the estimated average retail price would have reached US$2,060 — higher than the average price of any model ever released. He wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further driving up the average selling price and gross margin." In his view, amid rising memory prices, this would have been an important defensive measure.

Edison Lee also pointed out that Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are reasons for further downgrading the company's stock rating.

From Edison Lee's report, it is unclear whether he believes the entire redesign plan has been shelved, or only certain elements have been cancelled.

Top-voted comment by bcom77

It's quite possible that in the not-too-distant future, prices will soar to such absurd levels that consumers will simply stop buying new ones. Unless major tech companies seriously address the issue of component costs, their profit margins will start to decline sharply. They cannot keep passing on costs to consumers indefinitely.

For example, many people have long speculated that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island next year, making an "all-glass" screen simply impossible to achieve. But the rumoured quad-curved design may still be launched.

Regardless, if Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone design has indeed been cancelled, other credible sources should be able to confirm it soon.
